learning_outcomes.text: Analyze the operation of thermal machines and engines by applying the principles of thermodynamics and fluid mechanics, evaluating their energetic performance and efficiency under different operating conditions.

Select and dimension basic thermal equipment and installations, such as compressors, turbomachines, and thermal engines, considering technical, energetic, operational, and efficiency criteria for industrial applications.

syllabus_topics: Energy equation referred to fixed and moving systems.
Thermodynamic analysis of stages in turbines and compressors.
Rankine cycle: power, efficiency, and trends.
Modifications to the Rankine cycle: reheating and regeneration.
Operating parameters: indicated and effective parameters.
teaching_methods: Participatory lecture, conferences, company visits, fair attendance, etc.
Individual or group. Case resolution, role-playing, application exercises, oral and written presentations, debates, etc.
Activities performed in spaces with specialized equipment. Research sessions on classroom didactics.
Completion of a project to solve a problem or address a task through planning, design, and execution of a series of activities.
Personalized and small group attention. Instruction aimed at reviewing, redirecting class materials, learning, and completing assignments, etc. Specific student inquiries. Scheduled tutorials.
Individual and group preparation of essays, problem-solving, projects, etc., to be submitted and presented in practical classes.
Student study: preparation of readings, exam preparation, exercise elaboration, class preparation, etc.
assessment_rules: The subject is passed if the final grade is 5 points or higher, and no written part grade is below 4 points. In the first sitting, unapproved parts can be recovered. If written test scores are below 4, the subject is failed, and the final grade will be 'No Presentado' (if absent from the exam) or the score obtained. In the second sitting, Project Integrated grades are maintained. For students exempt from the Project Integrated, its weight will be transferred to the written tests.
